Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Food and Animal Sciences, Ph.D.
Return to: College of Agriculture
Program Overview
Mission of the College
The College of Agriculture carries out the Land Grant mandates of the University in teaching, research, and service. The major goal of the College is to satisfy the educational needs and aspirations of both traditional and non-traditional students enrolled in its academic programs.
Department Goals and Objectives
The graduate programs in the College of Agriculture are designed to provide students with a solid and the most relevant up-to-date curriculum that blends 21st-century leadership skills and scientific knowledge to solve problems in food, agriculture, and environmental sciences. Students develop the necessary skills and competencies and expand their knowledge, creativity, and scholastic activities through classroom instruction, experiential hands-on learning, and networking opportunities that prepare them for today’s ever-demanding job market, culminating in advanced research capabilities at the doctoral level.
Program Description
The Ph.D. in Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences is an interdisciplinary, research-based terminal degree designed to prepare students for advanced careers in food, agricultural, and environmental sciences and to meet the growing demand for research professionals in private industry, academia, and government agencies. The program integrates core STEM training with discipline-specific depth through three concentrations:
Plant Science - advanced training in plant biology, breeding, genetics, crop production, horticulture, and related plant-based sciences.
Food and Animal Sciences - training that integrates food sciences and the animal sciences, including food processing, food safety, product development, animal nutrition, animal production and management, and animal biotechnology.
Natural Resources - training in environmental sciences, natural resources management, ecology, soils, forestry, geospatial analysis, and climate-related disciplines.
The concentrations align students’ coursework and dissertation research with well-defined career pathways in food, agriculture, and environmental science, while the shared core ensures a common foundation in research methods, statistics, ethics, and scholarly communication. Candidates admitted to the program must have completed a research (thesis-based) M.S. degree.
Program Outcomes
Prepare students for advanced research careers in private industry, academia, and government.
Develop experts capable of independent research, critical analysis, and contribution to knowledge in food, agricultural, and environmental sciences.
Equip scholars with the ability to design, conduct, and disseminate original research that addresses significant problems in food, agricultural, or environmental systems.
Provide specialized doctoral training through three concentrations (Plant Science; Food and Animal Sciences; Natural Resources) aligned with current workforce needs.
Foster leaders who can contribute to policy development and innovation within the agricultural, food, and environmental sectors.
Cultivate a comprehensive understanding of the scientific, economic, and social dimensions of food, agricultural, and environmental sciences.
Admission Requirements
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year degree-granting college or university AND a thesis-based M.S. degree with a major in an agricultural, food, biological, environmental, or related science.
Minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale for the M.S. degree.
Minimum GRE score of 290 (Verbal + Quantitative, or Verbal, Quantitative & Subject).
A sliding scale for GPA and GRE may be used for minor deficiencies for degrees from U.S. institutions.
A faculty advisor must be identified prior to admission, and the advisor must accept the student. The advisor’s area of research must align with one of the three program concentrations (Plant Science; Food and Animal Sciences; Natural Resources).
International Students:
TOEFL minimum score: Internet-based Test (iBT) - 71 (Computer-based Test (CBT) - 197; Paper-based Test (PBT) - 530) OR IELTS minimum score of 6.0. Test scores are valid for five years.
Non-U.S. transcripts must be evaluated by a foreign educational credential agency (e.g., WES, ECE, …).
Required Application Materials (submitted via GradCAS): Official transcripts (B.S. and M.S.), GRE scores, three reference letters (from academic or research instiutions with proper letterheads), personal statement of purpose (SOP) describing research interests, intended concentration, and motivation, CV/Resume, and any supporting documents (e.g., publications).
Important Dates
Refer to the official 2026-2027 Graduate School Calendar when available. Ph.D. programs may have earlier deadlines.
Confirm specific deadlines for the Ph.D. in Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences with the Graduate School. Application deadlines for doctoral programs are typically earlier than master’s programs.
Program Duration
Ph.D. is typically 3-4 years post-Master’s.
Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) at the Ph.D. level is standard for 36 months.
Transfer of Credits: Up to 6 credit hours of Ph.D.-level coursework from another institution may be transferred if a passing grade was received and courses are deemed equivalent, subject to approval. M.S. courses cannot be transferred into the Ph.D. program.
Degree Requirements
Maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0.
Declare a concentration (Plant Science; Food and Animal Sciences; or Natural Resources) and file a program of study during the first semester of enrollment.
Complete the 13 credit hours of core courses (AGSC 5110, AGSC 6350, AGSC 6620, AGSC 7200, AGSC 7590, AGSC 7610, AGSC 7620) with a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Complete 11 credit hours of elective coursework approved by the advisory committee and selected from the elective pool for the student’s concentration.
Successfully defend the dissertation proposal.
Pass both written and oral comprehensive examinations to achieve Ph.D. candidacy.
Complete approved curriculum, doctoral seminars, and experiential learning courses.
Complete 24 credit hours of doctoral dissertation research (AGSC 8120) and successfully defend the dissertation.
Refer to the Agricultural Science Graduate Student Handbook for program milestones and timelines.
Total Credit Hours: 48
Core Courses: 13 credit hours
Electives (concentration-specific): 11 credit hours
Doctoral Dissertation Research: 24 credit hours
Accreditation Information
Tennessee State University is accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC). The Ph.D. in Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences is established within the existing doctoral program and is not subject to specialized programmatic accreditation at this time.
Career Opportunities
Graduates pursue careers as research scientists, university faculty, and leaders in government agencies (e.g., USDA, EPA, USDA NRCS) and in private food, agricultural, and environmental industries. Concentration-specific career paths include:
Plant Science: molecular genetics, plant breeding and crop improvement, horticulture, plant pathology, and biotechnology research positions in industry, academia, and government.
Food and Animal Sciences: food scientists, animal scientists, food safety and quality professionals, product development researchers, and R&D roles in the food and animal industries.
Natural Resources: environmental scientists, soil scientists, ecologists, foresters, geospatial analysts, and doctoral-level roles in federal agencies (e.g., USDA NRCS) addressing environmental and climate challenges.
Faculty Credentials
Graduate faculty across all departments within the College of Agriculture participate in the program, with student assignment based on research expertise aligned with the chosen concentration. Full graduate faculty membership is required to chair dissertation committees. Faculty members in the proposed concentration areas are nationally and internationally recognized and have ongoing USDA-funded and other extramurally funded research programs in state-of-the-art laboratories and facilities.

Program of Study and Credit Hours Required
The Ph.D. in Food, Agricultural and Environmental Sciences requires a total of 48 credit hours, consisting of 13 credit hours of core coursework (shared by all concentrations), 11 credit hours of concentration-specific electives, and 24 credit hours of doctoral dissertation research.

Required of all students regardless of concentration.

Concentrations and Electives: 11 Credit Hours
Students must complete 11 credit hours of electives selected-in consultation with the advisory committee-from the elective pool corresponding to their declared concentration.
Food and Animal Science Concentration
The Food and Animal Sciences concentration integrates research training in food science and animal science. Graduates are prepared for R&D, product development, and scientific leadership roles in the food and animal industries and for faculty and research positions in academia and government.
